messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Gabapentin is a prescription medicine.
Gabapentin is used to treat partial seizures.
Gabapentin is used to treat nerve pain from shingles.
Gabapentin is used to treat restless legs syndrome.
The restless legs syndrome treatment is for the Horizant brand only.
It may also be prescribed off-label for other conditions.
These conditions include diabetic nerve pain, anxiety, and fibromyalgia.
Gabapentin is thought to work by calming overactive nerve signals in the brain and nervous system.
It is an anticonvulsant and nerve pain medication from the drug class gabapentinoids
Gabapentin brand names are Neurontin, Gralise, Horizant, and Relgaabi.
These brand names may not be interchangeable.
Gabapentin is not a federally controlled substance.
Some states classify gabapentin as Schedule V.
Other states require gabapentin prescriptions to be reported to their prescription drug monitoring program.
Prescription drug monitoring programs are used to track prescriptions.
Rules on refills and quantity limits vary by state.
The most common side effects of gabapentin are dizziness.
Triplet: ["Gabapentin", "may be prescribed off label for", "other conditions"]

The relation 'may be prescribed off label for' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug may be prescribed for the condition specified by the object entity despite not being officially approved for it.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'may be less effective in': The subject drug may not work as well in patients with the condition or factor specified by the object entity.
B. 'does not act on': The subject drug does not exert its effects directly on the entity specified by the object entity.
C. 'not approved for': The subject drug is not approved or not recommended for use in the patient population specified by the object entity.
D. 'has example of unapproved use': The subject drug is associated with the specific method of use specified by the object entity as an example of unapproved use.
E. 'has other uses': The subject drug may be used for purposes that are not specified or listed in the provided medication guide.
F. None of the above.

Answer:
